verdicts.reason: A keeps the original structure and reading order, but it is a shrunk copy: the cans are small, the descriptors ('Bright & zesty', etc.) and can labels are tiny, and the three columns spread so wide that the middle of the canvas feels empty. B breaks the design. Flavor names are stacked away from their descriptors, and the descriptors no longer match the names (Honey Rosemary sits above 'Bright & zesty'). One can is huge while two leftover cans are shrunk and scattered next to a tiny, hard-to-read CTA, and the body copy is jammed under the headline.

A is the same faithful but shrunken layout: tiny secondary text and can labels, and a lot of empty space between the widely spaced columns. B at least gives the CTA a readable size, but it is crammed beside the logo at the top right, ahead of the headline. The flavor names are still separated from their descriptors, which are mismatched, and two tiny orphaned cans float at the bottom next to one oversized can, so the grouping and hierarchy are broken.
